rules.sentence: Infection typically occurs 6 to 8 weeks post-insertion and is more likely attributable to post-insertion care than to arterial colonization during the procedure.
IPC-related pleural infection often results in pleurodesis, particularly with staphylococcal infection.
There is no documented increase in the risk of pleural infection with IPCs in immunocompromised patients.
Patients treated with IPC for MPEs can develop painful nodules near the insertion site or the point of entry into the parietal pleura.
Mesothelioma is notorious for causing catheter tract metastasis.
